scopeNote: Statewide ballot measures for Georgia — November 3, 2026 General Election. Georgia does not have citizen initiative; all measures are legislature-referred. 2026 session Crossover Day is March 6, 2026. This manifest was generated February 25, 2026.

ballotMeasures.officialTitle: Georgia Increase Maximum Acreage of Bona Fide Conservation Use Property Amendment (2026)
ballotMeasures.certificationNote: Passed House 168-5 on March 6, 2025; passed Senate 50-1 on March 18, 2025. Certified for November 2026 ballot.
ballotMeasures.ballotQuestion: Shall the Constitution of Georgia, for the purpose of protecting family farmland, be amended so as to increase the maximum acreage to qualify for assessment and taxation as a bona fide conservation use property from 2,000 acres to 4,000 acres?
ballotMeasures.yesVoteMeans: Raise the max acreage cap for bona fide conservation use property from 2,000 to 4,000 acres per owner. Takes effect January 1, 2027.

ballotMeasures.officialTitle: Georgia Timber Standing Timber Ad Valorem Tax Exemption Amendment
ballotMeasures.certificationNote: In House Ways and Means Committee as of Feb 25, 2026. Crossover Day March 6.
ballotMeasures.yesVoteMeans: Exempt standing timber on forest land conservation use covenant parcels from ad valorem taxation at harvest or sale.
ballotMeasures.noVoteMeans: Standing timber continues to be subject to ad valorem taxation.

ballotMeasures.officialTitle: Georgia Probate Judge Nonpartisan Election Constitutional Amendment
ballotMeasures.certificationNote: Passed full House Feb 12, 2026. Now in Senate. Backed by Chief Justice. Strong near-term candidate.
ballotMeasures.yesVoteMeans: All probate court judges elected in nonpartisan elections statewide.
ballotMeasures.noVoteMeans: Counties retain option to hold partisan probate judge elections.

ballotMeasures.legislativeSource: HR 1114 (HOME Act, 2025-2026), House Speaker Jon Burns (R)
ballotMeasures.officialTitle: Georgia Homeownership Opportunity and Market Equalization (HOME) Act Constitutional Amendment
ballotMeasures.certificationNote: Filed Jan 29, 2026. Needs 2/3 vote (Republicans hold ~100 seats, need ~20 Democrats). $5B/year fiscal impact. Status uncertain.
ballotMeasures.yesVoteMeans: Phase in and eventually eliminate homestead property tax for primary residences by ~2032.
ballotMeasures.noVoteMeans: Georgia homeowners continue paying property taxes under existing law.

ballotMeasures.officialTitle: Georgia Affordable Housing Separate Property Tax Classification Constitutional Amendment
ballotMeasures.certificationNote: Still in House Ways and Means as of Feb 23, 2026. Low probability of making ballot.
ballotMeasures.yesVoteMeans: Create separate property tax classification for LIHTC-funded affordable housing at lower rate.
ballotMeasures.noVoteMeans: Affordable housing developments taxed under standard property tax rules.

failedMeasures.officialTitle: Georgia Sports Betting Constitutional Amendment Referendum
failedMeasures.certificationNote: Died without full House vote at 2025 Crossover Day. Re-introduced Jan 2026 with little momentum. Highly unlikely to reach voters.
